liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Fire On The Mountain** (2 reviews): The reviewer, at a first show while very young and drunk, remembers only this song; Jerry flubs words in verse one, but it is a hot version afterward [13][20]
- **Samson And Delilah** (1 review): Brent plays punchy fills during a strong, hot version [20]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (1 review): A wide-ranging out-of-Scarlet jam leads into a spot-on transition to Fire [20]
- **Lost Sailor** (1 review): Reviewer hears hypnotic playing from Jerry in this version [23]

## Setlist highlights

- **gd81-09-25 s1 t01 Crowd Tuning**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd81-09-25 s1 t02 New Minglewood Blues**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd81-09-25 s1 t03 Friend Of The Devil**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd81-09-25 s1 t04 El Paso**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd81-09-25 s1 t05 Peggy O**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd81-09-25 s1 t06 Little Red Rooster**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd81-09-25 s1 t07 Bird Song**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]
- **gd81-09-25 s1 t08 Beat It On Down the Line**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [24]

## The recordings

- **gd1981-09-25.140017.fob.senn421.streeter.miller.clugston.flac1644** (recommended): audience recording; 28 songs; 180 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd1981-09-25aud.weiner.23626.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 27 songs; 186 min; rated 3.5/5 by 2 [3]. Said about its sound: MD5 checksums for disc 1 track 7, Bird Song, fail to verify on this audience copy [22]
- **gd1981-09-25.178965.Shure.SM57.renninger.carbonetta.visser.flac24**: source not stated; 27 songs; 172 min [5]
- **gd81-09-25.sbd.clugston.2215.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 26 songs; 177 min; rated 4.11/5 by 18 [6]. Said about its sound: Lossless files sound good but carry a watery artifact, as if converted from an MP3; Reviewer finds the non-soundboard version crisper with better highs, and the soundboard muddy [14][16]
- **gd81-09-25.aud.jim.13725.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 26 songs; 183 min; rated 3.33/5 by 6 [7]. Said about its sound: The soundboard has almost no bass or drums; Jerry's guitar and Brent's tinny keyboard lick dominate; Around seven minutes into an intense jam, the soundboard has an odd-feeling splice or switch; The audience recording lets you hear some drums, and the reviewer prefers it to the soundboard [17][23]
- **gd1981-09-25.148686.sbd.latvala.nixon.clugston.flac16**: soundboard; 26 songs; 176 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [8]. Said about its sound: The first few minutes of New Minglewood Blues have mix issues [8]
- **gd1981-09-25.sbd.miller.88822.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 26 songs; 177 min; rated 3.91/5 by 11 [9]. Said about its sound: Uploader calls the recording poor, starting badly and getting worse; circulated only on request [9]

## Around the show

- The reviewer's first Dead show; it led to many more shows over the following fourteen years [13]
- A Lehigh freshman camped out the night before tickets went on sale and photographed the show [15]
- This was the first of a three-show East Coast run [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1981-09-25.140017.fob.senn421.streeter.miller.clugston.flac1644**: taped by Frank Streeter; transferred by Charlie Miller and Scott Clugston; source: Source Info: Frank Streeter's Master FOB Audience Cassette; Sennheiser 421 mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell MX90); Transfer Info: Cassette Master (Nakamichi CR-7A) >… [1]
- **gd1981-09-25aud.weiner.23626.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Steve Rolfe; transferred by Noah Weiner; source: Audience Recording: Nak 700's [3]
- **gd1981-09-25.178965.Shure.SM57.renninger.carbonetta.visser.flac24**: taped by Kenn Renninger; transferred by Nick Carbonetta, Eric Visser; source: Shure SM57 > Marantz Superscope [5]. Also: Beat It On Down The Line and Drums & Space patched from Jonathon Aizen's source; Cassettes come from the collection of taper and trader Kenn Renninger, shared by his wife Peg [5]
- **gd81-09-25.sbd.clugston.2215.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [6]. Also: An original 1981 audience tape from a Sig Phi member matches this file, though the tape cuts the last 20 seconds; Etree database discussion concluded this source has no MP3 generation, contradicting the claim of MP3-derived sound [15][18]
- **gd81-09-25.aud.jim.13725.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [7]
- **gd1981-09-25.148686.sbd.latvala.nixon.clugston.flac16**: taped by Dick Latvala; transferred by Greg Nixon and Scott Clugston; source: Master Soundboard Cassettes > Dick Latvala's Cassettes [8]. Also: Sourced from Dick Latvala's cassettes, transferred by Gregg Nixon, with patches from other sources; Streeter's Sennheiser 441 tape supplies the final 1:42 of The Music Never Stopped; a Nakamichi 300 fills Fire's last 3:39 [8]
- **gd1981-09-25.sbd.miller.88822.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Cassette Master -> Cassette -> CD [9]. Also: Soundboard with audience patches in The Music Never Stopped and Fire On The Mountain [9]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Jerry Garcia: [1981-09-25 Backstage Pass - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/image/1981-09-25-backstage-pass/) [25]
